jobs.description:

Legal & Professional Services

Ingenio is supporting a leading international law firm with the appointment of a Global Head of Digital Strategy & Transformation
.

This is a senior leadership position reporting directly to the Global Chief Operating Officer, with significant exposure to the Board and wider executive leadership team. The successful candidate will lead the firm's digital transformation strategy, bringing together business applications, data, AI, automation and digital client services to deliver measurable business improvements.

This is not a traditional IT infrastructure or operational technology role. An established CTO is responsible for those areas. The focus of this appointment is on strategy, development, transformation and execution
.

The Opportunity
You will take responsibility for developing and delivering a global digital transformation strategy across legal, corporate and trust services. Working with senior business stakeholders, you will turn commercial and operational challenges into practical technology solutions that improve efficiency, client experience and service delivery.

You'll inherit an established application development team and will be responsible for developing its capabilities as the transformation programme progresses.

Significant projects are already underway, including a major entity-management platform initiative, a broader data management and analytics programme, and opportunities to extend the use of AI and automation across the business.

Key Responsibilities
Develop and deliver a global digital strategy and transformation roadmap aligned with business priorities.
Lead and develop the existing Business Technology and Application Development team.
Own the business applications roadmap, including entity management and client-facing technology solutions.
Oversee the design, development and delivery of new systems, whether built internally, purchased or delivered through external partners.
Drive the data strategy, analytics, reporting and business intelligence agenda.
Identify and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across legal and professional services.

What We're Looking For
We are particularly interested in senior digital transformation and business technology leaders from professional services, legal, fiduciary/corporate services, financial services or similarly complex, regulated environments
.

You will bring:
Significant experience leading digital strategy, business technology or enterprise transformation.
A proven track record of delivering complex technology programmes with measurable business outcomes.
Strong experience across business applications, software development and technology-enabled process improvement.
A solid understanding of data strategy, analytics, business intelligence, AI and automation.
Experience leading multidisciplinary development teams and managing external delivery partners.
The ability to influence Board-level stakeholders while remaining technically credible and close to delivery.

Location & Package
Toronto is the mandatory location, with this being an in-office role.

Interested?
This is an opportunity to shape the digital direction of an established international professional services organisation, with direct access to senior leadership, an existing development capability and significant transformation programmes already underway.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Michelle Queally at Ingenio
, or apply directly.

About Us

At CSDS, we prioritize people
—both within our team and in the communities we serve. Our mission is to redefine how Nova Scotians engage with government by creating accessible, reliable digital solutions centered around user needs.

In today’s tech-driven world, CSDS empowers government departments with essential digital solutions to meet Nova Scotians’ expectations.
As a trusted partner across government, we enable departments to fulfill their mandates with secure, user-friendly services. From healthcare and education to public safety, we collaborate to transform how services are designed and delivered.

We don’t just implement technology; we modernize outdated systems and reimagine processes.
Our agile, data-driven approach ensures that digital services are both efficient and adaptable to Nova Scotia’s evolving needs.

Joining CSDS means contributing to work that makes a real difference.
From providing vital tech support to healthcare professionals to strengthening cybersecurity and developing scalable digital platforms, you’ll play a key role in building a more inclusive, responsive government for Nova Scotians.

Together, we’re setting new standards for digital public service, delivering resilient solutions that meet today’s needs—and anticipate tomorrow’s challenges.

About Our Opportunity

Are you a collaborative, forward-looking leader who can turn complex health-system needs into clear digital pathways and better outcomes? Digital Solutions helps health initiatives move safely from early idea through design, review, approval, implementation, and production readiness. The team works across CSDS, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health, the Department of Health and Wellness, vendors, and other partners to shape solution design, strengthen architecture and governance, reduce risk, and coordinate dependencies across the broader digital health environment.

As Director, Digital Solutions, you will provide strategic and operational leadership for the team responsible for digital-health intake, business analysis, solution architecture, service navigation, and early delivery enablement. Reporting to the Executive Director of Digital Health Enablement, you will create the conditions for multidisciplinary teams to deliver secure, scalable, user-centred solutions that support clinical care, health-system transformation, and improved experiences for patients, providers, and partners.

You will bring structure to ambiguity, establish trusted relationships, and ensure initiatives receive timely guidance on technical design, architecture review, security and privacy alignment, procurement, operational readiness, and enterprise dependencies. Your leadership will help partners make informed decisions earlier, prevent avoidable redesign, and move priority work forward with greater clarity and confidence.

Primary Accountabilities

Provide senior leadership and oversight for the Digital Solutions portfolio, setting clear priorities and ensuring work is aligned with departmental, health-system, and enterprise objectives.
Lead and support managers, solution architects, business analysts, and other multidisciplinary resources, creating an empowered, inclusive, accountable, and delivery-focused team culture.
Oversee the intake, assessment, and early shaping of digital-health initiatives, ensuring partners receive practical guidance to define needs, clarify outcomes, identify dependencies, and determine the appropriate delivery and approval pathway.
Guide initiatives through solution design, architecture review, security and privacy alignment, procurement and contractual considerations, implementation planning, production readiness, and transition to operational support.
Provide advice and recommendations to the Executive Director Digital Health Enablement and senior government and health-system leaders, translating complex technical, delivery, financial, and operational issues into clear options, risks, and decisions.
Build and maintain strong partnerships across CSDS, Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health, the Department of Health and Wellness, other public-sector organisations, vendors, and jurisdictional partners.
Ensure effective portfolio governance, including prioritisation, risk and issue management, escalation, performance visibility, resource planning, and accountability for commitments.
Champion human-centred, iterative, and continuous-improvement approaches, helping teams adopt modern digital practices and respond effectively to changing requirements.
Work collaboratively to identify opportunities for innovation, reuse, standardisation, automation, and increased value across the digital-health ecosystem.
Provide sound stewardship of human and financial resources, including workforce planning, performance management, budget oversight, forecasting, procurement support, and value-for-money recommendations.
Represent Digital Health Enablement in governance forums, partner engagements, working groups, and cross-sector planning activities, promoting a connected and system-wide approach to digital-health delivery.

How You Can Make An Impact

Enable safer and more effective digital-health delivery by engaging early, resolving uncertainty, and reducing downstream risk and rework.
Improve the end-to-end partner experience by making CSDS pathways, requirements, decisions, and accountabilities easier to understand and navigate.
Help major health initiatives move from concept to implementation with stronger alignment across technology, clinical needs, operations, security, privacy, procurement, and vendors.
Build an engaged team that is trusted for its judgement, responsiveness, collaboration, and ability to create a practical path forward.
Advance digital enablement that contributes to better healthcare experiences and outcomes for Nova Scotians.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a credible and collaborative people leader with strategic leadership experience and a demonstrated record of delivery in complex environments. You are comfortable working across executive, operational, clinical, business, and technical settings, and you can translate competing needs into focused action.

Progressive leadership experience in digital delivery, information technology, health informatics, service transformation, business analysis, enterprise or solution architecture, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary and cross-functional teams, including internal employees, external resources, partners, and vendors.
Experience overseeing a portfolio of complex initiatives and balancing strategic priorities, operational pressures, delivery risk, and changing requirements.
A strong understanding of digital solutions and how technology, data, architecture, security, privacy, procurement, and operations come together to enable sustainable services.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and bring together diverse partners to reach constructive outcomes.
Experience providing clear, concise, and evidence-informed advice to senior leaders and decision-making bodies.
Experience with governance, prioritisation, risk management, financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor management, and service improvement.
Knowledge of modern digital and internet-era practices, including human-centred design, agile and iterative delivery, product or service thinking, and continuous improvement.
Excellent communication, facilitation, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex information accessible to varied audiences.
Demonstrated commitment to service excellence, respect, integrity, diversity, accountability, and the public good.

An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered. Experience in healthcare, digital health, government, or another complex regulated environment would be considered an asset.

jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

This role will require a deep understanding of both financial processes and cash management best practices, as well as the ability to drive operational excellence and delivery efficiency.  This role has accountability directly to the SVP & CIO of Group Functions Technology and to provide services to the heads of the various Group Finance Functions and their teams including the VP, Chief Accountant as well the SVP & Treasurer.

Lead and engage a large finance team through a period of transition, providing visible leadership, clarity, coaching and direction while maintaining operational continuity.
Assess the current finance operating model, capabilities, processes and priorities, identifying opportunities to enhance the effectiveness and value of the function.
Lead a complex organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring appropriate financial discipline while improving the quality of planning, assumptions and scenario analysis.
Strengthen management reporting and financial analytics, ensuring senior leaders have more timely, relevant and actionable information to support decision-making.
Improve the organization's approach to financial metrics, KPIs and performance reporting, creating greater visibility into organizational performance and impact.

A stable, engaged and well-led finance team positioned for the next stage of the organization's growth.
A clearer understanding of the capabilities, structure and priorities required within finance going forward.
A more robust and effective budgeting and forecasting process.
Significantly improved management reporting and financial insight.
More meaningful financial and operational metrics supporting executive decision-making.
Greater value being generated from existing ERP, reporting and data capabilities.
Stronger relationships between finance and operational leadership.
A finance function increasingly viewed as a strategic partner to the organization rather than simply a reporting and transactional function.
Clear recommendations for the continued modernization and evolution of finance beyond the interim mandate.

CPA designation is mandatory.

This assignment will particularly suit an executive who has "seen the movie before."

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.

Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
